Separate painting department / atelier **Tasvir Khana** of **100+ painters** under **Abdus Samad**; painting karkhanas at **Agra, Fatehpur Sikri, Lahore**; frescoes at Fatehpur Sikri; mostly **illustrated manuscripts** (Hamzanama, Tutinama, Akbarnama, Razmnama) and **portraits**; 3-D figures, foreshortening; Persian style became Indianised

**Zenith / golden age** of Mughal painting; shift from illustrated manuscripts to **albums and individual portraits**; events of his own life, **birds, flowers, animals** (naturalism); his own private atelier, a keen judge who could name the artist of a painting; decorated margins; **halo (nimbus)** behind the emperor's head; patronised European and Persian art
More interested in **architecture**; formal court scenes, albums (muraqqas), floral borders, more **gold and silver**, artificial stillness; painters Mir Hashim, Anup, Chitra
Opposed pictorial art, **withdrew patronage** → painters moved to provincial courts (Awadh, Hyderabad, Mysore, Bengal), Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar → fed the Rajput and Pahari schools

4.x: **Zenith under Jahangir** – Akbar built the atelier, Shah Jahan preferred architecture; **Jahangir mainly patronised painting**.
**Shift from illustrated manuscripts to albums and individual portraits = Jahangir**; **foundation laid by Humayun**.
Subjects of Mughal painting: **battle scenes, animals-birds-nature, court scenes**.

European pictures reached **Akbar's court through the Portuguese (Jesuit priests)** → **portraiture** and **smaller distant objects for spatial depth**; Mughal style = muted naturalistic colour, perspective and shading. So **European painting was introduced in Akbar's court** – not under Jahangir by **Danish merchants**.

The **first Jesuit mission from Goa** reached Akbar in **1580**: Father **Rudolf Acquaviva** with Father **Antonio Monserrate** and Brother Francis Henriques; they brought the **Polyglot Bible**, whose pictures Akbar showed to his painters.
